correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the all-parameter argument. For a feasible signed winding on each petal the nonnegative step counts are (ℓ_j±qw_j)/2; every arbitrary hub color and compatible collection of words gives one map. An internal move exchanges adjacent opposite signs, and a hub move exchanges first and last opposite signs on every petal, so winding is cellwise constant. The absence of a target square prevents adjacent source vertices from both varying in a cell; target degree two gives cubes, with disjoint adjacent-step exchanges at fixed hub. Identify the words with monotone paths in the rectangular grid, so the exchanges toggle ideal elements and a cube toggles an antichain of available elements. Deleting a maximal element of the poset removes a product strip attached along one end over the subcomplex containing all its predecessors; retracting each strip proves contractibility, including the degenerate one-word and prescribed-end cases. A hub cell with colors h,h+2 fixes all neighboring vertices at h+1, requiring both signs in each petal. Its nonempty fixed-end interface is contractible and the cell piece is precisely that interface times an interval. Thus a boundary winding sector splits into q contractible fixed-hub fibers; in strict sectors the vertex fibers and edge interfaces replace by points by CW homotopy gluing. The resulting step-two graph has one cycle for odd q and two for even q≥6. These facts establish the products and the empty case integrally. A direct independently written bounded enumeration for (6,4)→C₆ gave 792 maps: the (0,0) sector has 720 vertices in the two hub-parity components, with mod-2 b₁=2 in total, and each (±1,0) sector has 36 vertices in six fixed-hub components, with b₁=0. Each frozen fixed-hub component has six vertices, six edges and one filled square; hence frozen here does not mean isolated. Bounded b₁ and component counts corroborate, not replace, the proof.
residual_risks: The product expression is for ordinary homotopy type, not homeomorphism, and its point summands need not be isolated vertices. The proof requires q≥5 and exactly one common hub.

evidence: The cycle-codomain theorem gives the point/circle dichotomy for any connected source, and detects the point type by a directed cycle in the edge orientation induced by +1 modulo q. The square-free-codomain theorem includes cycle targets and gives component types. Wrochna tests reachability between specified maps via groupoid, parity and tight walks.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For a bouquet the only simple source cycles are petals, so the directed-cycle criterion detects a fully monotone petal and supplies the type independently. It does not count feasible windings, identify how the hub-color alternatives connect in each sector, or sum the resulting point and circle counts.

evidence: A single winding with any extremal petal freezes the hub in an otherwise possibly deformable product of petal complexes. E.g. with (6,4)→C₆ there are 12 contractible components even though the 4-cycle contributes only strict windings, and 2 circles rather than the four one would get by multiplying the two strict per-petal component counts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The component-type theorem or a direct product of prior single-cycle counts does not imply the formula by parameter substitution. One needs a joint interface argument or equivalent synchronized reachability computation to count sectors and hub phases, which is the substantive family calculation.

evidence: A bouquet can be formulated as the fiber product of the single-cycle complexes over their common hub-color evaluation: all petals must allow the same hub color(s). The earlier generalized-theta record instead keeps two distinct terminals and counts common displacements at fixed relative windings.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Independent choices occur in the fixed-hub fibers, not in unbased connected components. Identifying two theta terminals is a new color constraint, not a permitted substitution in its numerical theorem; that theorem also restricts to odd target cycles.

value.rationale: This is a natural cut-vertex extension of cycle-to-cycle reconfiguration, with explicit integer counts for arbitrary petal number and lengths. The hub can move only when all petals can move it at once, even though nonhub recoloring can persist when the hub is frozen. The formula captures that distinction and even/odd hub-phase connectivity without enumerating maps, and gives the homotopy type rather than just a test on individual components.
residual_risks: The assertion does not extend to general cactus assemblies, two-terminal sources by simple substitution, or the square target.
